definitions.explanation: A heartfelt, honest attitude; loyalty and trustworthiness in one's words and actions. A core virtue in traditional Japanese ethics, often associated with bushidō and Confucian values.
What is actually the case; truth as opposed to falsehood. Somewhat literary or formal; everyday speech uses {本当|ほんとう} instead.

examples.english: To act with sincerity / give one's all faithfully.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{誠|まこと}のある{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He is a person of integrity.

examples.japanese: お{客様|きゃくさま}には{誠|まこと}をもって{対応|たいおう}します。
examples.english: We respond to customers with utmost sincerity.

examples.japanese: {今|いま}{語|かた}ったことは{全|すべ}て{誠|まこと}である。
examples.english: Everything I just told you is the truth.

examples.japanese: {噂|うわさ}が{誠|まこと}か{偽|いつわ}りか、まだ{確|たし}かめていない。
examples.english: I haven't yet verified whether the rumor is true or false.

notes:
An older native Japanese word that has taken on a somewhat formal or literary tone in modern usage. Also a very common given name (especially masculine).

ADVERBIAL USE — {誠|まこと}に:
The most frequent modern usage is as the adverb {誠|まこと}に (truly, sincerely, indeed), heard in polite business expressions:
- {誠|まこと}にありがとうございます: thank you very much (sincerely)
- {誠|まこと}に{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません: I am truly sorry
- {誠|まこと}に{恐縮|きょうしゅく}ですが: I am truly sorry to trouble you

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {誠|まこと}を{尽|つ}くす: to act with utmost sincerity
- {誠|まこと}を{込|こ}める: to put one's heart into
- {誠|まこと}のある{人|ひと}: a person of integrity

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {真実|しんじつ}: truth — modern, neutral word for truth; more common than {誠|まこと} for sense 2
- {誠実|せいじつ}: sincere; faithful — the な-adjective form covering the same virtue
- {本当|ほんとう}: true; really — everyday equivalent of sense 2
